toolChanges.reason: Java-focused linter (103 patterns) on a repository with no Java code — confirmed 0 issues at baseline. Pure wrong-stack noise; replaced in coverage by PMD7's much smaller, actually-relevant ruleset.

Legacy ESLint 8 (.eslintrc-style). Project's package.json declares eslint ^10.6.0, and there is no .eslintrc/.eslintrc.* in the repo, so ESLint9 (flat-config, closer version match) supersedes it. Kept only ESLint9 to avoid running two overlapping JS/TS linters.

Duplicative Python meta-linter wrapper — its findings (bandit/pycodestyle/mccabe checks) overlap with the standalone Bandit and Pylint tools already enabled. Only unique output was a single mccabe complexity hit, already covered by Lizard.

New tool added for Python (fast, modern linter) as part of the stack-tailored config. Note: the repo has a committed .codacy/generated/Ruff/ruff.toml, so Codacy Cloud runs this tool in Configuration File mode — only 3 patterns are actually cloud-managed; the rest are governed by that file (see conflicts).

Flat-config ESLint matching the project's actual eslint devDependency version. Same Configuration File caveat as Ruff applies: the repo has a committed .codacy/tools-configs/eslint.config.mjs, so only 3 patterns are cloud-managed.
New tool for YAML/JSON schema linting, part of the stack-tailored auto config.

New Infrastructure-as-Code security scanner covering the repo's Dockerfile and YAML/compose files — expands security coverage into IaC misconfigurations, an area the prior 14-tool config had no dedicated tool for.

Newer PMD engine, but only 4 patterns actually apply to this stack (1 ECMAScript error-prone rule, 1 XML rule; the other 2 are Maven/pom-specific and irrelevant but harmless at 0 matches). Replaces the old Java-heavy PMD tool.

patternChanges.reason: Attempted to disable (Info severity, pure CodeStyle, 5 instances of intentional late imports in main.py/script_stats.py) but rejected with 409 — Ruff runs in Configuration File mode for this repo. See conflicts.

keyImprovements: Removed 3 tools that were pure noise or redundant: PMD (103 Java-only patterns, 0 relevant issues on this Python/JS repo), legacy ESLint 8 (166 patterns, superseded by ESLint9 which matches the project's actual eslint ^10.6.0 dependency), and Prospector (4 patterns duplicating Bandit/Pylint/Lizard findings).

Trimmed Semgrep from 1605 to 895 enabled patterns by removing ~710 patterns for languages entirely absent from the repo (Java, Ruby, Go, Scala, Kotlin, C#, PHP, Rust, Clojure, Swift, Elixir, Apex) — zero issue-count impact since none of those ever matched, but a large reduction in scan surface and future noise risk.
Added Checkov (IaC security scanner) for the repo's Dockerfile/YAML — genuinely new security coverage the prior config lacked.

4 new legitimate JavaScript/JSON Security findings surfaced from Semgrep's expanded selection (incomplete sanitization before use, insecure Object.assign, insecure WebSocket usage, risky npm dependency version ranges) — kept per security-caution guidance rather than cut just to shrink the headline count.

This pass was only possible because the repo's 'Default coding standard' was unlinked mid-session — before that, every one of the 14 previously-enabled tools and their patterns were locked (enabledBy the standard), and all repo-level changes would have been rejected with 409.

conflicts.reason: Repo has a committed .codacy/generated/Ruff/ruff.toml, so Codacy Cloud defers to it instead of cloud-managed patterns. Blocked attempt: disabling Ruff_E402_module-import-not-at-top-of-file (5 Info-severity CodeStyle issues). To reduce this noise, edit ruff.toml directly (or remove it from the repo if it isn't meant to be authoritative) rather than through Codacy.

Repo has a committed .codacy/tools-configs/eslint.config.mjs, so Codacy Cloud defers to it instead of cloud-managed patterns; only 3 patterns remain cloud-configurable.
